newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on soybean gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on soybean gains.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended higher on Monday, lifted by gains in soybeans tied to forecasts for hot, dry weather this weekend in the U.S. Midwest, pit sources said.

Meteorologists said cooler temperatures would move into the Corn Belt this week, followed by a hot, dry weekend. Long-range forecasts suggested the heat wave would persist through early next week with no significant moisture, Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino said.
Nearby soymeal struggled with reports that China had cancelled 150,000 tonnes of old crop soymeal purchases.
Traders there said China had purchased more than 500,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for roughly $300 a tonne, C and F, but had started to default after soymeal prices fell to about $270 a tonne, C and F.
Meanwhile, there was talk China was buying 200,000 tonnes of U.S. new crop soybeans. U.S. exporters could not confirm the deal but said it was likely China would be inquiring.
Soymeal ended $6.50 to $2.80 per ton higher with December up $5.60 at $202.20. Soyoil closed 0.30 to 0.17 cent per lb higher with December up 0.24 at 22.15.

On the day, Refco Inc was a key buyer of soymeal, accounting for 400 lots in the December, 200 January and 300 March. Smith Barney bought 200 December and 100 August and sold 100 December and 300 March. ADM, R.J. O'Brien and E.D. and F. Man International each sold 300 August and Cargill Inc sold 300 September and 100 August.
In soyoil, Cargill sold 200 August and 100 January while Refco, Produce Grain and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp each bought 200 December, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 40,000 lots, above Friday's actual volume of 21,328. Soyoil volume was pegged at 30,000 lots, against Friday's 14,064.
